The '''Spanish Premiere Two-Player Game rules booklet''' is a 20-page Spanish-language Decipher rules booklet for the [[Premiere Two-Player Introductory Game]]. The surviving copy is a scan of a printer proof: every page has crop marks and a Quark-style production slug reading '''SP 2 PLRY BOOKLET 7/2/98'''.<ref name="fb-sergio">[https://www.facebook.com/groups/starwarsccg/permalink/10159018539903127/ SWCCG Two-Player Game Rulesbook (Spanish).pdf], Sergio Domenech, Star Wars CCG Facebook group (8 September 2021). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/swccg-spanish-2pg-rules-booklet-1998 Internet Archive]; [[:File:Spanish_Premiere_Two-Player_Game_rules_booklet.pdf]].</ref> [[Sergio Domenech]] (Red Squadron 49, Madrid) posted that scan to the Star Wars CCG Facebook group on 8 September 2021.

The English Two-Player box shipped in February 1996 (Parker Brothers in North America; Waddingtons in Europe). Takara printed a Japanese Two-Player game. Encyclopedia 3.2 records further language editions that were planned and never released.<ref name="encyc">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p.201 (Other Foreign Language Releases) and p.29 (Premiere Two-Player). Collecting hub: [https://www.starwarsccg.org/collecting/ starwarsccg.org/collecting/].</ref> This booklet is the Spanish-language rules proof for the Two-Player product. Decipher's May 1999 product library lists the English Premiere Two-Player Introductory Set and does not list a Spanish SKU.<ref name="library">[https://web.archive.org/web/19990504174938/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/productlibrary/thecollection/index.html Star Wars Customizable Card Game : The Expansions], Decipher.com product library (archive, 4 May 1999).</ref>

== Artifact ==

The Facebook PDF is 20 pages, A4 (596×841 pt), image-only, with empty Info metadata. The running header on page 1 is `SP 2 PLRY BOOKLET 7/2/98 10:40 PM Page 1`; later pages stamp 10:41 PM. SP is Spanish, 2 PLRY is Two-Player, BOOKLET is the rules booklet, and 7/2/98 is 2 July 1998.

|- style="background:transparent; border:none; vertical-align:bottom;"
| style="border:none; text-align:center;" | [[File:Spanish-2PG-rules-p01-cover.png|260px|Cover]]<br />''Cover: ''Juego introductorio para dos jugadores'' / ''Libro de reglas'''''
| style="border:none; text-align:center;" | [[File:Spanish-2PG-rules-p19-copyright.png|260px|Copyright page]]<br />''Page 19 copyright and Decipher contact block''

The cover uses the same STAR WARS Customizable Card Game art language as the English Premiere Two-Player booklet, with the Spanish subtitle '''JUEGO INTRODUCTORIO PARA DOS JUGADORES''' and footer '''LIBRO DE REGLAS'''.

Page 19 carries TM & © 1998 Lucasfilm Ltd. and © 1998 Decipher Inc., Norfolk, Virginia, authorized by Lucasfilm. The contact block is Decipher Inc., 253 Granby Street, Norfolk, Virginia 23510-1817, telephone (757) 623-3600, RebelBestLeader@decipher.com, FTP ftp.decipher.com, WWW www.decipher.com, plus CustomerService@decipher.com, the Game Information Exchange (GIX), Game Company Support (GCS), and (757) 420-NEWS. The manufacturing line is incomplete English: '''Fabricado in the USA'''.

The full scan is [[:File:Spanish_Premiere_Two-Player_Game_rules_booklet.pdf]] and [https://archive.org/details/swccg-spanish-2pg-rules-booklet-1998 Internet Archive].

== Contents ==

[[File:Spanish-2PG-rules-p02-intro.png|360px|Introduction page]]

Page 2 names the game '''''Guerra de las Galaxias: Juego de Cartas Coleccionables (SW-JCC)'''''. The box described there matches the English Two-Player product: two 60-card decks (Light with the Rebel symbol on the back, Dark with the Imperial symbol), a 15-card Premiere expansion pack drawn from the 324-card Premiere set, and six cards unique to this Two-Player set (Luke, Vader, two interrupts, two locations).

[[File:Spanish-2PG-rules-p03-quickstart.png|360px|Quick-start card tables]]

Page 3 is a 20-card quick-start for each side. Printed titles mix Spanish translations with English leftovers:

* Translated: Mina de Tiempo ([[Timer Mine]]), Barrera Imperial ([[Imperial Barrier]]), Barrera Rebelde ([[Rebel Barrier]]), ¡Corre Luke, Corre! ([[Run Luke, Run!]]), Obsesión de Vader ([[Vader's Obsession]]), Estrella de la Muerte: Nivel 6, Pasillo Del Reactor Principal ([[Death Star: Level 6 Core Shaft Corridor]]).
* Left in English: Jawa, Blaster, LIN-V8K, LIN-V8M, Kintan Strider.

[[File:Spanish-2PG-rules-p11-starship.png|360px|Starship anatomy]]

Page 11 teaches starship anatomy with an '''English-language''' scan of [[Imperial-Class Star Destroyer]] and Spanish callouts (Nombre, Número de destino, Leyenda, Blindaje o Maniobra, Poder, Enlace Scomp, Coste de despliegue, Valor de renuncia).

[[File:Spanish-2PG-rules-p20-phases.png|360px|Turn phases on the back cover]]

The back cover lists the six phases in Spanish: Activar, Control, Despliegue, Batalla, Mover, Robar.

== Language editions ==

Japanese Takara printed Premiere, [[A New Hope]], [[Hoth]], and both Two-Player games. Encyclopedia 3.2, page 201, under Other Foreign Language Releases: additional language releases were planned beyond those Japanese sets, and anime-style cards were considered for Japan. Those further languages were not released.<ref name="encyc" />

The 2 July 1998 slug on this booklet sits in the [[Jabba's Palace]] / [[Second Anthology]] / Revised A New Hope window, two years after the English Two-Player box (February 1996) and in the same year Takara's later Japanese Two-Player and Hoth printings carry a 1998 copyright.

Decipher Squadron Members in Spain promoted the English game: Sergio Domenech in Madrid (Red 49 FL), Guillermo Ruiz in Barcelona (Red 42 / Gold 17), and Unai Herran in Zaragoza (Red 48).<ref name="sm">[https://www.starwarsccg.org/decipher-swccg-squadron-members/ Decipher SWCCG Squadron Members], starwarsccg.org. Fan-site table: [https://www.geocities.ws/plarathas/SMs.html geocities.ws/plarathas/SMs.html]. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20160409152825/http://reocities.com/collegepark/plaza/9433/SMs.html Wayback, 9 April 2016].</ref> On 10 October 2012 a Spanish hobby thread on labsk.net said SWCCG had little acceptance in Spain, perhaps because it was only in English.<ref name="labsk">[https://labsk.net/index.php?topic=95165.msg973702 Star Wars CCG, rediseñado], labsk.net, LeBastard (10 October 2012).</ref>

CardGuide Wiki tags Star Wars CCG as Language English, Japanese, Spanish and lists Premiere Limited OTHER LANGUAGES ES JP. Its [[Premiere Limited (Star Wars CCG) (ES)]] page is a title-translation checklist (machine-style Spanish titles, empty packaging, Language field left English).<ref name="cardguide-es">[https://cardguide.fandom.com/wiki/Premiere_Limited_(Star_Wars_CCG)_(ES) Premiere Limited (Star Wars CCG) (ES)], CardGuide Wiki. [https://cardguide.fandom.com/wiki/Star_Wars_CCG Star Wars CCG] at CardGuide Wiki.</ref> That checklist is a fan table of translated names, not a photograph of a Spanish print run.

== Related Spanish-language documents ==

Players Committee PDFs titled ''gameterms_en_espanol.pdf'' and ''ds2_expansion_rules_en_espanol.pdf'' are 2009 fan translations by Renato Tenorio. They use '''Juego de Cartas Seleccionables''' for the game name. This 1998 booklet uses '''Juego de Cartas Coleccionables (SW-JCC)'''. Those PC files are a later volunteer glossary, not this Decipher proof.<ref name="tenorio">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/wp/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/gameterms_en_espanol.pdf Equivalencias inglés – español], Renato Tenorio, version 1.5 (© 2009). Index: [https://www.starwarsccg.org/rules/ starwarsccg.org/rules/].</ref>
